message.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
               <jats:p>Stellar bow shock nebulae are arcuate shock fronts formed by the interaction of radiation-driven stellar winds and the relative motion of the ambient interstellar material. Stellar bow shock nebulae provide a promising means to measure wind-driven mass loss, independent of other established methods. In this work, we characterize the stellar sources at the center of bow shock nebulae drawn from all-sky catalogs of 24 <jats:italic>μ</jats:italic>m–selected nebulae. We obtain new, low-resolution blue optical spectra for 104 stars and measure stellar parameters temperature <jats:italic>T</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>eff</jats:sub>, surface gravity <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi>log</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>g</mml:mi>
                     </mml:math>

                  </jats:inline-formula>, and projected rotational broadening <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi>v</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>sin</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>i</mml:mi>
                     </mml:math>

                  </jats:inline-formula>. We perform additional photometric analysis to measure stellar radius <jats:italic>R</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>*</jats:sub>, luminosity <jats:italic>L</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>*</jats:sub>, and visual-band extinction <jats:italic>A</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>
                     <jats:italic>V</jats:italic>
                  </jats:sub>. All but one of our targets are O and early B stars, with temperatures ranging from <jats:italic>T </jats:italic>= 16.5 to 46.8 kK, gravities from <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi>log</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>g</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                     </mml:math>

                  </jats:inline-formula>2.57 to 4.60, and <jats:inline-formula>
                     <jats:tex-math>

</jats:tex-math>
                     <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" overflow="scroll">
                        <mml:mi>v</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>sin</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>i</mml:mi>
                     </mml:math>

                  </jats:inline-formula> from <100 to 400 km s<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>. With the exception of rapid rotator <jats:italic>ζ</jats:italic> Oph, bow shock stars do not rotate at or near critical velocities. At least 60 of 103 (60%) OB bow shock stars are binaries, consistent with the multiplicity fraction of other OB samples. The sample shows a runaway fraction of 23%, with 19 stars having <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
                  <jats:sub>2D</jats:sub> ≥ 25 km s<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>. Of the 19 runaways, at least 15 (≥79%) are binaries, favoring dynamical ejection over the binary supernova channel for producing runaways. We provide a comprehensive census of stellar parameters for bow shock stars, useful as a foundation for determining the mass-loss rates for OB-type stars—one of the single most critical factors in stellar evolution governing the production of neutron stars and black holes.</jats:p>
title: Fundamental Parameters for Central Stars of 103 Infrared Bow Shock Nebulae
